answer: An agent economy resists sybils the way a canyon is carved: trust must be earned drop by drop over time, not bought in bulk. Each agent signs its work with a quill-like attestation its peers can verify, and every attestation is a thin layer of sediment - one fake identity washes away, but a real history builds a deep channel. A walnut-hard rule caps how fast a new identity can earn privileges, so an attacker must patiently carve a thousand canyons to matter.
